results.title: Solar panels, dynamic tariffs, domestic hot water and EV charging - Page 4 - openHAB Community
results.content:
A shortcut and my advice to you would be to either use it as an adapter like I do or NOT to go EVCC at all. If you get a charger that can be properly controlled through an openHAB binding like for example an e-go, then it’s not hard to implement the surplus charging inside openHAB.  
Plus, remember in winter you will not want that mode but charge based on power price. You could reuse most of your heat pump code for that. [...] Since it fits perfectly with what’s being discussed here (solar surplus, dynamic tariffs, heat pump optimization, and EV routing), I’m presenting my EMS binding to the forum. It runs entirely on your existing items and even has a “shadow mode” so you can test its logic safely without it actually triggering any of your physical devices.

Anybody is welcome to have a look, ask, try, and I’m open to any ideas!

Here are the links:

EMS Manager: 

OCPP repo: [...] Cheers,  
Markus

As I said earlier, as soon as you have more than one HEMS, it’s getting very complicated.  
Every hybrid inverter controls battery charging so it is a HEMS, too. EVCC is another one, and so is your heat pump optimizer.  
Your #3 is mandatory for hybrid inverters as they cannot properly charge the battery without the meter info, that’s why every hybrid inverter is sold+installed in a bundle with a compatible meter.  
For your other questions, the answer is mostly “no”.
